A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same contamination-detection survey and LLMSanitize library paper. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–5 report original LLMSanitize evaluations, including detector results, dataset-overlap measurements, and comparisons between base and instruction-tuned models.

after.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 retain the authors' guided-prompting and sharded-likelihood evaluations. These remain original empirical results; Appendix A supplies usage instructions rather than additional outcomes.

M1.justification: No change to the authors' detection procedures is established. The checker classes are renamed to match the open-data/closed-data terminology, and implementation examples are expanded. Newly discussed detectors such as DICE are surveyed methods from other work.

E1.justification: V2 retains the six OpenLLM benchmarks but removes the known-data training-versus-validation/test overlap evaluation and the March 2024 BBC news scenario. This eliminates a distinct detection task and a clean-data evaluation domain. The new appendix examples report no outcomes that restore this coverage.

E2.justification: The empirical comparison drops Min-K% Prob and the six open-data methods evaluated in v1 Table 4: GPT-2-style, GPT-3-style, exact match, PaLM-style, GPT-4-style, and Platypus-style detection. Guided Prompting and Sharded Likelihood remain. Newly surveyed detectors are not added empirical comparators.

E3.justification: V2 removes the full-partition overlap evaluation, the base-versus-instruction-tuned comparison design, and the contamination-free BBC control. Retained evaluations still specify 100 test examples and four 7B model families, with GPT-3.5-turbo additionally used for guided prompting. The PDFs do not establish reruns or changed settings for the retained scores.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix B and Table 5 compare guided-prompting detections before and after instruction tuning across four model families and six benchmarks. V2 removes this analysis entirely, losing the direct investigation of detection sensitivity to instruction tuning.

E5.justification: Both versions report p-values and visually distinguish statistically nonsignificant results for Guided Prompting and Sharded Likelihood. Neither reports seeds or repeated-run counts for these experiments. Fewer result entries do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 54 per-benchmark p-values carried from v1 Tables 1–2 into v2 Table 1 are identical. However, v2 removes the Min-20% Prob scores, direct-overlap percentages, base-model results, BBC results, and cross-benchmark averages. These are substantial result removals, not performance changes under retained settings.

T1.justification: Section 3 narrows the setup from a model-specific training set that could be unknown to one explicitly inaccessible to researchers. This revises the access assumption underlying the taxonomy. The overlap-based contamination target remains unchanged, and no theorems, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The survey and library remain the central contributions. V2 narrows the abstract and introduction toward contamination detection and defines the headline classification through training-data accessibility, replacing the less precise data/model contamination distinction. The first-survey and general-purpose-library claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds limitations of temporal evaluation: maintaining fresh datasets is difficult, and post-cutoff code performance need not decrease. Conversely, v1 Appendix B's discussion of instruction-tuning effects and the corresponding detector-robustness limitation disappears. Most Section 4 recommendations and future challenges remain.

D1.justification: V2 replaces minimal pseudocode with detailed Appendix A instructions covering LLMSanitize 0.0.8 installation, Python 3.9/CUDA 11.8, argument examples, a two-GPU vLLM setup, streaming, and logging. The listed code link changes to a temporary anonymous repository. V1's explicit statement that the main experiments use chatbot versions is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the closed-data review through membership-inference foundations, cloze-based detection, Cao et al.'s cutoff counterexample, Xu et al.'s benchmark-leakage work, and DICE. It also acknowledges a concurrent contamination survey, while removing Lee et al.'s deduplication discussion and some background citations. These changes extend the substantive research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial survey passages are rewritten. Section 3 replaces the nested Model Completion organization with separate memorization, confidence, and model-based sections; Section 4.2 gains evaluation categories. Experimental appendices are replaced by a usage appendix, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column formatting. Figure 1 is redrawn with a revised hierarchy and expanded entries. V1 Tables 1–2 are merged into a compact v2 Table 1, Tables 3–5 disappear, and formatted code listings are added in Appendix A.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the access-based taxonomy, expands substantive survey coverage, and provides much more useful library instructions. However, it removes original evidence for open-data detection, a detector comparison, clean-data controls, and sensitivity to instruction tuning without replacement analyses. For this combined survey-and-library paper, the gains in clarity and usability and losses in empirical support do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
